what_its_for: Ublituximab-xiiy is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults. This includes clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting MS, and active secondary progressive MS. It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) and slows the worsening of disability by targeting and reducing certain immune cells (B cells) that attack the nervous system.
how_to_take: This medication is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion directly into your vein by a healthcare provider in a clinic or infusion center. You will NOT give this medication to yourself at home. Each infusion session takes about 1 hour. You will be monitored during and after your infusion for any reactions. Before each infusion, your doctor or nurse will give you medications such as a steroid, antihistamine, and fever reducer to help prevent infusion reactions.
dosing: The usual dosing schedule is: First dose: 150 mg given as one IV infusion. Second dose: 450 mg given about 2 weeks after your first dose. After that: 450 mg given once every 6 months. Always keep your infusion appointments. Your doctor may adjust your schedule based on your health.
missed_dose: If you miss or need to reschedule your infusion appointment, call your doctor or infusion center as soon as possible. Do not wait until your next scheduled dose. Your doctor will help you reschedule and get back on track. Try to avoid going long periods without your medication, as this can allow MS activity to return.
storage: This medication is stored and prepared by healthcare professionals at the infusion center. You do not need to store it at home. If you are curious, the medication vials are kept refrigerated between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C) and protected from light until they are used.
what_to_avoid: Avoid live vaccines (such as MMR, chickenpox, shingles live vaccine, or nasal flu spray) while taking this medication and for a period after stopping, as your immune system will be weakened. Talk to your doctor about getting any vaccines you may need at least 4 weeks BEFORE starting treatment. Avoid close contact with people who are sick, as you may be more likely to get infections. Tell your doctor about all other medications, vitamins, and supplements you take, especially other MS treatments or immune-suppressing drugs.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience: fever, chills, rash, or trouble breathing during or after your infusion (signs of an infusion reaction); signs of infection such as fever, cough, pain with urination, or feeling very unwell; symptoms of a serious brain infection called PML, including confusion, memory problems, vision changes, weakness, or difficulty speaking or walking; sores or blisters on your skin or mouth (possible viral infection); unusual bruising or bleeding; or if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding.
when_it_works: Ublituximab-xiiy begins to reduce the B cells in your immune system within days of your first infusion. However, the full benefit for controlling your MS relapses and slowing disability may take weeks to months to notice. It is important to continue your treatment even if you feel well, as the medication works best when taken on schedule.
special_populations: Pregnancy: This medication may harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for 6 months after your last dose. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medication passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Older adults: Older patients may have a higher risk of infections. Your doctor will monitor you closely. Patients with infections: Do not start this medication if you have an active infection. Your doctor will check for infections, including hepatitis B, before starting treatment. Patients with liver or kidney problems: Tell your doctor about any liver or kidney conditions, as they may affect your care plan.
